article.Citation/Title: Dusen, W. V., Wilson, W., Miners, W., & Hook, H. (1967). Treatment of alcoholism with lysergide. Quarterly Journal of Studies on Alcohol, 28(2), 295-304.
article.InterventionDescription: Oral lysergide (mean 400ug, range 100-800), given to 1-4 women at a time in a private day-hall setting with music and art; 1-3 sessions, each with an assigned therapist.

ae_events.Description: Asthmatic attack occurring during a lysergide session, leading to early termination of the session.
Epileptic seizure occurring during a lysergide session, leading to early termination of the session.
A disturbed emotional reaction during a lysergide session, severe enough to require early termination of the session.

article.Outcome: Primary comparison selected as the 18-month row of Table 2 (the longest follow-up horizon reported for all groups), comparing the PRELYSERGIDE historical-control group (N=37 header) to the LYSERGIDE EXPERIMENT group (N=56 header, the pooled 1-, 2- and 3-session subjects). Value taken verbatim from the Abstract, which restates Table 2's numbers in prose: 'the average score of the control group was 4.03... and of the lysergide group, 3.97' (on the 2=worse/3=same/4=improved/5=much-improved scale). The 'Pilot Lysergide' column (3.70, N=15) was not used as the primary arm because the pilot phase was explicitly an uncontrolled, exploratory dose-finding period ('In this period we experimented with dose levels and setting to obtain maximum positive results'), whereas the 'Lysergide Experiment' group (1-,2-,3-session subjects equated on age and Mindlin Index) is the article's actual controlled comparison and the one the Results section's chi-square/Duncan's-range-test statement addresses ('there was no significant difference between any of these groups'). This is a non-obvious judgment call; a reviewer could reasonably argue for pooling all 71 lysergide-treated women (pilot + experiment) against the 37 controls instead.
article.SD: No dispersion or test-statistic value is printed for this specific two-group (prelysergide vs. lysergide-experiment) comparison. The article states only that 'the groups were compared by chi-square test and Duncan's range test (14), a variant of the analysis of variance. At the 5% level there was no significant difference between any of these groups' -- no chi-square value, F value, or degrees of freedom are given anywhere for this comparison. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: No exact p-value or printed threshold symbol (e.g. '<.05') accompanies this comparison. The article states directly 'there was no significant difference between any of these groups-indeed the differences did not even approach significance,' which is narrative non-significance language. Per the anti-conversion rule, this is recorded as 'NS' verbatim rather than converted to a numeric threshold.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Coded '.' because the exact number of subjects whose scores produced the 18-month means (4.03 and 3.97) is not stated as an integer -- Table 2 gives only '% Followed' (76% for prelysergide, 63% for lysergide-experiment) alongside the group header N's (37 and 56), and back-calculating (0.76x37=28.1; 0.63x56=35.3) would fabricate false integer precision from rounded percentages. There is also an unresolved internal inconsistency in the source text: the Method section states 'We could then compare results on 28 prelysergide controls, 15 pilot lysergide patients, 29 given 1 lysergide session, 18 given 2 sessions, and 9 given 3 sessions, a total of 99 subjects' (28+15+29+18+9=99), whereas both the Abstract ('a control group of 37 women') and Table 2's own header ('PRELYSERGIDE (N=37)') give 37, not 28, for the same group (37+71=108, not 99). Per the instruction to report inconsistent numbers as printed rather than construct a decoding theory, this discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved, and no single confident integer is asserted for SampleSize_NFinal.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 12/14 criteria met. Not described: eligibility (only a brief screening statement is given -- 'the grossly brain damaged, prepsychotic, and emotionally severely disturbed were screened out' -- with no formal inclusion/exclusion list covering diagnostic thresholds, age limits, or medical comorbidities; Table 1's age range of 23-64 is descriptive sample data, not a stated entry criterion); sample_size_power (no a priori or post hoc power calculation or sample-size justification anywhere). Met: objective and design (Method opens with the study's purpose and describes the pilot/control/experimental phases); setting (Mendocino State Hospital, 1,600 alcoholics/year, the day-hall session room described in detail); intervention and comparator (dose, session structure, and the prelysergide historical-baseline comparator are all described, including the abandoned double-blind scopolamine attempt); outcomes (the 4-point Much improved/Improved/Unchanged/Worse rating scale is defined); randomization and blinding (both are described, including as abandoned -- 'we abandoned the double-blind control after running five subjects' -- which satisfies 'described, including when described as absent'); statistical_methods and results (chi-square, Duncan's range test, and Pearson correlations are named and results reported in Table 2 and text); harms ('three sessions were terminated early because of the subject's reaction-an asthmatic attack, an epileptic seizure, and a disturbed emotional reaction' is an explicit statement, even though not in a dedicated section); funding_coi ('This study was supported by a research grant from the California Department of Mental Hygiene'). n_met=12 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 0 (null/negative). The article states directly 'the lysergide subjects were not noticeably more sober than those treated before lysergide,' and the 18-month mean for the lysergide-experiment group (3.97) was numerically lower than the prelysergide control group (4.03). No comparison across groups approached significance ('did not even approach significance'). The Conclusion reiterates 'we did not demonstrate increased sobriety.'
article.Clincial Trial YN: 1, consistent with the eligibility screen: a prospectively planned lysergide intervention with defined enrollment (71 women across pilot/1-/2-/3-session groups), an assigned regimen (number of lysergide sessions), and prospective outcome assessment at 6, 12 and 18 months post-hospitalization.
article.RandomizationYN: 0. The design that produced the reported Outcome data was not randomized: 1-, 2- and 3-session subjects were 'equated on the basis of age and the Mindlin Prognostic Index' (matching, not random allocation), and the prelysergide comparison group is a non-concurrent historical cohort. The article does describe an earlier, abandoned attempt at true random assignment (scopolamine vs. lysergide, 'subjects were to be assigned by a person outside the study'), but this was stopped after only 5 subjects due to unblinding and is not the source of any reported outcome data. Coded 0, not 3, per the boundary-case rule that an absent design element is 0.
article.BlindingYN: 0. The planned double-blind procedure was explicitly abandoned: 'we abandoned the double-blind control after running five subjects... too small for reliable conclusions.' No blinding was in place for the data reported in Table 2.
article.Double+Blind: 0, consistent with BlindingYN=0 per the field's must-not-contradict rule.
article.Comparator: 1. A non-concurrent (historical) control group of 37 women 'who had been in the same program just prior to the addition of lysergide to the treatment' serves as the comparator, explicitly described as substituting for the abandoned randomized/blinded control ('To substitute for the missing control group we began following up 37 women...'). This is judged an active-comparator/historical-control design, not a design where the concept does not apply, so it is coded 1 rather than 3 or 0.
article.PrimaryCare: 0. All treatment occurred on an inpatient state-hospital alcoholism unit (Mendocino State Hospital); no aspect of the study interfaces with primary-care settings or providers.
article.Power: 0. No a priori or post hoc statistical power calculation or discussion appears anywhere in the article.
article.Retention (%): 68. Directly stated in the Follow-Up section: 'Social service field workers and our own staff attempted to trace the outcome in all subjects at 6, 12 and 18 months after hospitalization... They were able to find 68% of all the subjects.' Denominator is the enrolled cohort (the study was not randomized, so per the codebook rule enrolled N is the denominator). Used directly rather than recalculated because it is the article's own aggregate figure; the per-group, per-timepoint '% Followed' cells in Table 2 range from 61% to 80% (the 80% cell is 12-month Pilot Lysergide), so this overall 68% figure sits within that range. Not within 2 points of 80 itself, so no additional near-threshold flag applies to the value used.
article.ConfoundYN: 1. The article substantively examines potential confounding/prognostic factors against outcome: Pearson correlations of follow-up results with age (.21), history of delirium tremens (.05), history of arrests (-.02), length of time drinking had interfered with life pattern (.17), the Mindlin Prognostic Index (+.22), and diagnosis ('Diagnosis showed no relationship to outcome'). None were found significant, but the assessment itself satisfies the field.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: 0. Only a brief screening statement is given -- 'the grossly brain damaged, prepsychotic, and emotionally severely disturbed were screened out to remove some not likely to benefit or those who might be disturbed further' -- with no accompanying formal inclusion criteria (diagnostic thresholds, age limits) or a stated exclusion list beyond this one sentence. Judged not to constitute 'clearly stated' inclusion/exclusion criteria, consistent with how comparably brief screening mentions were treated in other pre-1980 articles in this corpus.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: 0. The primary alcohol-outcome measure is a 4-point scale (Much improved/Improved/Unchanged/Worse) devised by the investigators themselves with no validation citation. The Blewett Scale of Psychedelic Reactions (used) and the Mindlin Prognostic Index (used as a covariate, cited to ref. 13) are both validated instruments, but neither is used to measure the alcohol/SUD outcome itself -- the Blewett Scale characterizes the drug experience, and the Mindlin Index is a prognostic/matching covariate, not an outcome measure.
article.Funding/COI YN: 1. 'This study was supported by a research grant from the California Department of Mental Hygiene' (footnote 1). No separate conflict-of-interest statement is given, but funding-source disclosure alone satisfies this field.
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.'. No severity descriptor (Mild/Moderate/Severe) or severity-mapping language for the alcoholism diagnosis is given anywhere; Table 1 gives only descriptive statistics (mean years of excessive drinking, number of DTs, number of arrests) without a stated severity classification.
article.Age_Median: Bracket '30-50', from Table 1's Total column: 'Mean years 41.4' (range 23-64), corroborated by the Abstract's 'Their mean age was 41 years.' Note that Table 1 (headed Pilot/1-Dose/2-Dose/3-Dose/Total/Range) reports baseline characteristics only for the 71 lysergide-treated women; no age data is reported anywhere for the 37-woman prelysergide historical-control group. Age_Median therefore reflects the lysergide-exposed cohort, the group with reported baseline data.
article.PercentFem: 100. 'Our patients were all women' (opening paragraph, contrasting with the mostly-male Canadian studies), and the Abstract separately confirms 'a control group of 37 women' -- both the lysergide-treated and prelysergide-control cohorts were entirely female.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Coded '.': race/ethnicity of the sample is never reported anywhere in the article.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: 0. No income, occupational, insurance, or other SES information is reported for the sample. 'Economic resources' and 'occupational level' are named only as component factors of the Mindlin Prognostic Index scale (a prognosis-matching covariate), not as reported descriptive characteristics of the study sample.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: US. Mendocino State Hospital, Talmage, California (author affiliations; 'a hospital that admits 1,600 alcoholics in a year').
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: 1, judgment call. Subjects were routine admissions to a state-hospital alcoholism unit that 'admits 1,600 alcoholics in a year' and 'learned of the experiment from each other and from the investigators' -- a real-world clinical inpatient population rather than an externally recruited research sample. Caveat: participation was voluntary ('when they volunteered for the experiment') and the 'grossly brain damaged, prepsychotic, and emotionally severely disturbed' were screened out, which narrows representativeness somewhat.
article.InterventionDescription: Summarized from the Sessions/Method sections: oral lysergide, mean dose 400ug (range 100-800), given to 1-4 women at a time (average 2) in a private day-hall setting with music, art, and privacy screens; 1, 2 or 3 sessions per subject, each with an assigned staff therapist present before, during and after.
article.InterventionTherapy: 1. Each subject was 'assigned a staff member who worked with them before, during and after the experience,' subjects were 'vigorously counseled to cooperate with the experience,' and 'much that emerged in the session was worked through with staff in the days following' -- integration/preparation support beyond drug administration alone.
article.HarmsAssessed: 1, consistent with SafetyReported='Y'. The article explicitly reports that 'only three sessions were terminated early because of the subject's reaction-an asthmatic attack, an epileptic seizure, and a disturbed emotional reaction,' and states the investigators' approach to managing such reactions -- an explicit statement about adverse reactions during the intervention, judged sufficient per the instruction that the distinction between 'no AEs occurred' and 'authors never looked' is the one thing to get right, and to avoid understating harm.
article.Followup in months: 18. Follow-up was conducted 'at 6, 12 and 18 months after hospitalization' (Table 2); 18 months is the longest reported horizon and is reported for all three groups (prelysergide, pilot, lysergide-experiment).
article.BehaviorChangeMeasured: 1. The core outcome scale directly measures drinking behavior: 'Much improved: Complete abstinence or only drinking very small quantities. Improved: Definite reduction of alcohol intake.'
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: 0. No biomarker, physiological measure, or vital-sign outcome is reported as a study outcome for the alcohol-treatment analysis (the psychiatrist 'was prepared to adjust the dose' during sessions is procedural, not an outcome measure).
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: 0, judgment call. The four written-account rating scales (A: personal-life engagement, B: naturalness of expression, C: emotional intensity, D: degree of transcendence) characterize the phenomenology of the lysergide experience itself, not a depression/anxiety/PTSD/well-being outcome instrument; no such mental-health outcome scale is applied to the participants as a treatment-outcome measure.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: 0. No dedicated quality-of-life instrument is used. The informal notes on being 'more productive at home or in social relationships' and 'more stable and productive at work' are part of the qualitative follow-up rating, not a validated QoL measure.
article.Implementation Outcome: 0. No feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, reach, adoption, or sustainability outcome is discussed; the pilot phase's dose-titration purpose is not framed or measured as an implementation outcome.
article.ReductionMeasured: 1. 'Improved: Definite reduction of alcohol intake' is a distinct rating-scale category from complete abstinence, satisfying the partial-reduction outcome definition.
article.CessationMeasured: 1. 'Much improved: Complete abstinence or only drinking very small quantities' directly measures cessation.
article.RelapseMeasured: 1, judgment call. Relapse is embedded in the outcome scale's definition ('Unchanged: No fundamental change or temporary improvement and relapse') and is explicitly discussed in the Results: 'alcoholics could look very good one week and be quite drunk the next.' Coded 1 because relapse/return-to-use is an explicit part of what the follow-up rating tracked, though it is not a separately reported standalone metric.
article.MortalityMeasured: 0. Mortality is never addressed as an outcome or otherwise anywhere in the article.
article.LSD: 1. Lysergide (LSD) is the sole psychedelic intervention administered.
article.OtherPsychedelic: 0. Scopolamine, used only in the brief abandoned double-blind control arm (5 subjects, no outcome data reported from it), is a non-psychedelic anticholinergic control agent, not a psychedelic, and sets no substance flag.
article.SafetyReported: Y. The article contains an explicit statement about adverse reactions during dosing sessions: 'Only three sessions were terminated early because of the subject's reaction-an asthmatic attack, an epileptic seizure, and a disturbed emotional reaction. We learned to deal with disturbed reactions and would later have been willing to work through seizures or any other kind of reaction.' This is judged an explicit safety-relevant statement even though it is not set off in a dedicated Adverse Events section.
article.AnyAEReported: Y, per the three session-terminating reactions described above.
article.NumDistinctAEs: 3 distinct AE types: asthmatic attack, epileptic seizure, disturbed emotional reaction, each named once in 'an asthmatic attack, an epileptic seizure, and a disturbed emotional reaction.'
article.NParticipantsWithAE: 3, judgment call. The text describes 'three sessions... terminated' for three named reactions, most naturally read as three distinct patients (one event type per terminated session); the article does not state whether any single patient experienced more than one of the three events, so 3 is the most parsimonious reading and is flagged here as an assumption.
article.AE_denominator: 71, the full lysergide-exposed cohort (15 pilot + 29 one-session + 18 two-session + 9 three-session). The three terminated-session events are described in the general Sessions section covering the whole treated cohort's protocol, not restricted to a named subgroup, and no more specific AE-assessment population is stated, so the full exposed cohort is used as the denominator.
article.ArmScope: psychedelic_arm. All three reported AE-like events occurred during lysergide dosing sessions; the historical prelysergide comparison group received no lysergide and reports no AE data.
article.WorstSeverity: Severe, the maximum across the three ae_events (epileptic seizure graded Severe per the rubric's explicit PAT-specific severe-event list).
article.EligibleYN: Y. (a) Clinical trial: a prospectively planned lysergide intervention with defined enrollment, an assigned session-count regimen, and prospective 6/12/18-month outcome assessment -- passes. (b) SUD outcome: the primary outcome scale directly measures abstinence/reduction of alcohol intake -- passes.

ae_events.Dusen 1967_AE01: Severity graded Moderate under the assumption that ending the session constituted active intervention (satisfying the rubric's 'requires active intervention... but meets no FDA seriousness criterion' Moderate band), but the article gives no detail on medical management, duration, or outcome of the asthmatic attack beyond 'terminated early because of the subject's reaction.' SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because this is a genuine under-specified-AE case per the rubric's default-Mild-unless-signal-present rule; here the session-termination signal itself supports at least Moderate, but insufficient detail exists to rule out a more serious reading, so it is flagged for human review rather than silently absorbed.
ae_events.Dusen 1967_AE02: Graded Severe per the severity rubric's explicit statement that seizure is a PAT-specific event that is Severe by default ('suicidal behavior/attempt, psychosis..., seizure, serious cardiovascular event, hospitalization, HPPD... or any event the authors themselves label an SAE'). SeveritySource='rubric' because this is a 1967 article -- CTCAE did not exist, and the authors used no formal grading language, only narrative description ('an epileptic seizure'). SeverityIndeterminate='N' because the rubric provides an unambiguous categorical default for this event type regardless of the article's sparse descriptive detail.
ae_events.Dusen 1967_AE03: The 'disturbed emotional reaction' is coded AE_type='both' because it plausibly reflects challenging-experience phenomenology (per the rubric's core adaptation principle, expected in-session distress is graded by consequence/intervention need, not intensity) that in this case had a clinical consequence (session termination). Graded Moderate on the signal that the session was actively terminated, but SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because no detail is given on the reaction's specific content, duration, or resolution beyond termination and the authors' general statement that they 'learned to deal with disturbed reactions' in later cases -- insufficient detail to confirm whether this met any FDA seriousness criterion or resolved without further intervention.

config_proposal.measure: 4.03 vs 3.97 (18-month mean outcome score, 2=worse...5=much improved scale; prelysergide control N=37 vs Lysergide Experiment N=56)
config_proposal.note: The primary comparison (prelysergide control vs. lysergide-experiment group at 18 months) is reported only as two group means on an ordinal 4-point scale, with no paired dispersion statistic, chi-square/F value, or exact p-value printed for this specific comparison (only the narrative 'did not even approach significance' across all groups). None of the seven supported conversion methods (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR) applies without a printed test statistic or a group-level proportion breakdown, so no defensible conversion exists.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: The lysergide-experiment group's 18-month mean (3.97) is numerically lower than the prelysergide historical-control group's (4.03), and the article states differences across all groups 'did not even approach significance' by chi-square and Duncan's range test; the study's own conclusion is that lysergide 'did not increase the patients' abstinence.'
